item: The erase calls the main database encrypted only on positive evidence and names one of three states
summary: A header that is not SQLite's was enough for the erase to call the main database encrypted, skip its body and say the corpus was unrecoverable; a plaintext store whose page 1 an earlier failed erase randomised reads exactly so. Now: this process read the very pinned file under a key (connect.opened_with_key, by device and inode, never persisted, forgotten on a plaintext open) keeps the encrypted path; everything else takes the plaintext path (fast destruction, unlink, body rewrite) and the verdict is settled after page 1 and the log are destroyed. SQLite's header is not encrypted whatever any record says; another header plus the app's at_rest_encryption.json naming this very (device, inode), read no-follow through the pinned folder handle, regular file, at most 64 KiB, and a complete fast destruction is encrypted (no body rewrite); every other case is could not be determined, with the full rewrite and the R815 (3) note. The record gets the identity only after a real keyed page read by the app's engine (stat by path, atomic, removed on a plaintext open, a failed write never fails the open; additive per R755) and is destroyed with its store (an app file, R806). corpus_encryption in the report; the CLI, the HTTP answer and the page say encrypted and key destroyed, not encrypted, or could not be determined; an unknown store is never called unencrypted (strings x12).
